messages.subject: stan and distributed computing
parts:
Apologies if I'm asking a far too general question but I was wondering if there is a guide/ tutorial to using rstan on AWS, or atleast a linux cluster. The important outcome I'm hoping for is to use MORE than one machine. (I'm assuming that rstan already uses all available cores).

So far this is the best I could find but doesn't really go through examples:
http://www.r-bloggers.com/set-up-rstan-on-amazon-ec2/

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] stan and distributed computing

Not that we distribute. Each cluster works differently, so

Let us know if you find something written up that works.

- Bob

messages.author: 4b681bcd9d4d425d
messages.subject: Re: stan and distributed computing
parts:
The r-bloggers tutorial seems like a good way to set up a single remote EC2 machine with RStan. Following that, you can use any of the regular Stan models via command line RStan on that remote machine - it's not distributing the analysis among multiple machines, though - that would be harder.

You can then run one chain per EC2 computer, and combine them afterwards; how to do this is detailed here; https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/c8wb87yQkPc/Cb7mWSDgeWkJ (The task of sampling each chain doesn't parallelize, at least in the current architecture,, so it's not really useful to have a larger network except to sample more chains.)

Cheers,
David
